title: GCP-6.5: slot-claim rate limiting absent in all stacks (10/min/peer + 60/min global, silent drop)
close_reason: DONE: slot-claim rate limiting landed in ALL three stacks (spec/08:281 GCP-6.5: at most 10 claims/min per peer IID and 60/min globally, exceeding claims MUST be silently dropped). (1) RUST: lichen-gateway slot.rs SlotClaimRateLimiter (sliding window 60s, 10/peer, 60/global, HashMap<Iid, Vec<monotonic-ms>>) wired into handle_post_slots (resources.rs:1886, silently drops via empty 2.04 before replay state consumption) — unit tests in tests/slot_rate_limiter.rs 4/4 green. (2) PYTHON: SlotClaimRateLimiter in gateway/slot_claim.py (:320) with the same 10/60 limits wired via verify_slot_claim's rate_limiter param — tests in test_slot_claim.py (RATE_LIMITED reason asserted, :1073). (3) C: coap_slot_coord.c now has a bounded sliding-window rate limiter (commit 3b61dea089) — peer table 32 IIDs with per-peer stamps ring (max 10 in-window), global ring (max 60), mutex-guarded, keyed on the decoded claim's gateway_iid (payload key 5 == COSE kid); wired into slots_post before process_claim so rate-exceeded claims are silently discarded without consuming replay state. Verification: coap_slot_claim host suite 1/1 green with the limiter compiled in; gateway lib 252 green; python slot-claim tests green. The remaining C-side integration detail (peer IIDs learned via announces rather than claim decode) is a d7hg-family follow-up; the limiter itself is correct and self-contained.
